dossier.public_summary: The dips are much deeper in some TESS sectors than in others and odd and even dips differ by more than a factor of three, which is typical of an eclipsing binary folded at half its true period rather than a planet. The signal is not steady, so a planet on the target star is not the best explanation.

reasons.why: A very large odd/even depth difference much deeper odd transits favours a binary at twice the period (25.2 d), not a planet at 12.6 d.
Depth changes by a factor of ~7 between sectors.

Even the QLP light curve alone is not consistent: sector 19 as TESS-SPOC is ~2236 ppm but QLP sectors range ~9447 to ~16097 ppm, so the change is astrophysical/pipeline systematics rather than a steady planet.
